newsitem.title: CHINA: China shares indices end up on confidence.
newsitem.headline: China shares indices end up on confidence.

text.p: China's A and B share indices ended up on Monday with domestic investors confident in the short-term stability of the market and on positive forecasts for China's economic outlook, brokers said.
Shanghai's B share index ended up 0.972 points or 1.45 percent at 68.129 points while Shenzhen's B index rose 2.49 points or 1.62 percent at 155.63 points.
Shanghai brokers said market sentiment was strong because there were no signs of political instability after the death of Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping last month.
Gains in H shares, Chinese firms listed in Hong Kong, added confidence to the B share market, they said.
"The advance was based on optimism about China's 1997 economic outlook," said Xu Yinhui, a Shenzhen analyst with China Guotai Securities Co Ltd.
China's 1997 budget was announced in Beijing on Sunday, and included a gross domestic product (GDP) growth target of 8.0 percent and a retail price inflation target of 6.0 percent.
"Beijing is likely to lower bank interest rates if it is confident of capping retail price inflation below six percent," Xu said.
On the Shanghai B share market, stationery maker Shanghai Hero was the star performer after it posted strong 1996 results announced on Saturday, brokers said.
The stock rose $0.028 or 6.73 percent to $0.444 on volume of 675,200 shares.

Toy maker Shanghai Haixin was the most active and became the second biggest gainer on talk of good results for 1996, brokers said. It added $0.030 or 6.12 percent to $0.520 on volume of 1.3 million shares.
In Shenzhen, retailer Shenzhen International Enterprise B share was the strongest performer, gaining HK$0.29 or 5.57 percent to HK$5.50 (US$0.71) on trade of 680,100 shares.
Analysts said they expected the firm to post strong profits for 1996 on real estate investments.
Appliance maker Tsann Kuen traded most actively on 2.08 million shares, putting on HK$0.10 to HK$3.88.

Shanghai's A share index rose 24.033 points or 2.21 percent to 1,111.456 points and Shenzhen's A index surged 15.59 points or 4.08 percent to end at 398.22 points. The Shenzhen index has risen for seven consecutive trading days.
On Shanghai's A share market, Shanghai Tyre and Rubber was the biggest gainer on news that one of its projects had been chosen as a key project for the city in 1997, brokers said.
The stock surged 1.06 yuan to end at a 10-percent limit-up of 11.62 yuan (US$1.4) on volume of 1.0 million shares.
